statements.statement: A variable typed as 'any' can hold a string, a number, or any other value without causing a type error.
statements.explanation: The 'any' type turns off type checking entirely, so the variable accepts any value with no errors.

statements.statement: Using 'any' is the recommended way to type variables in TypeScript.
statements.explanation: Using 'any' defeats the purpose of TypeScript. It is an escape hatch for rare situations, not a go-to solution.

statements.statement: TypeScript will report an error if you call a method that does not exist on an 'any' variable.
statements.explanation: Because 'any' disables type checking, TypeScript will not flag invalid method calls. The error would only appear at runtime.
